text_content: read collapsed callawa bridge part of 2017 dpwh project a bridge in purok 2 barangay callawa buhangin davao city collapsed following heavy rains and flooding since monday night disrupting access for residents and motorists in the area photos circulating on social media showed portions of the bridge giving way as strong floodwaters battered the creek below amid continuous downpour documents shared with the media identified the structure as part of a department of public works and highways dpwh project under contract id 17lo 0133 for the concreting/widening/improvement of bypass road at buhangin-tigatto-mandug-callawa-fatima road including reconstruction of callawa bridge and rrow in davao city's 2nd district the contract was signed on may 11 2017 during the term of then davao city 2nd district representative vincent garcia and awarded by dpwh region 11 to premium megastructures inc with a total contract cost of p184,588,193.30 and a completion period of 240 calendar days the agreement was signed on behalf of the government by then dpwh 11 oic-regional director allan borromeo dpwh 11 spokesperson dean ortiz said the approximately 15 meter bridge had been affected by worsening erosion over the years due to the widening of the creek beneath it which was further aggravated by continuous heavy rains and strong flood currents since monday night the creek widened significantly over the years eroding the bridge approaches until the structure could no longer withstand the pressure from the floodwaters ortiz said no injuries or casualties were reported authorities are assessing the damage and monitoring other flood-affected areas in davao city contributed photos

text_content: flood in obrero 1960s i am taking a quick break from my work speaking of the heavy flood it reminds me of something here is a photo of some residents in obrero at the corner of clarin and porras streets during the flood this photo comes from the contributor's grandmother's family album the scene was possibly taken in the 1960s we learn from historian antonio figueroa that barrio obrero had its beginnings in the pre-commonwealth period the idea was to set aside parcels of land to be developed into villages for working men and let me tell you a collective memory from my personal journal about obrero's surrounding areas in old maps of davao the area from trading boulevard sta ana agdao all the way to obrero was a swampy or marshy and mangrove area in fact in ubalde and r castillo roads there were plenty of pagatpat trees at high tide seawater would come in bringing with it fish like ibis bugaong wild tilapia and the water snake called tangkig of course there were also crabs like kuray katang and alimango in obrero alone sometime in the past some college students who stayed in boarding houses fondly recalled how they would put their shoes in a basin floating in dirty water so they could wear them the next morning i wonder how many parts of the city have still experienced flooding since the 1960s or even earlier i want to learn from urban planners and the two young men from the right they are so wet in the rain neil teves author's note photo courtesy of the bonifacio and ermitania delute family albums contributed by neil gementiza photo first posted by paul corpus on november 2 2019 for educational purposes

text_content: time to act agusan basin davao floods signs of impending disaster by manny piñol in october of 2016 president rody duterte visited the typhoon devastated cagayan valley region he warned that unless the mighty cagayan river is dredged soon a disaster could happen inn the low-lying towns along the country's longest river the president said that soil erosion in the denuded mountains of the region ravaged by illegal logging operations have resulted in the heavy siltation of the meandering river causing it to overflow every time the rainy season or typhoons come the president's grim warning came true last week not in cagayan valley but at least five areas in mindanao where soil erosion from bald mountains have caused heavy siltation and flash floods flash floods and inundations occurred in cagayan de oro and misamis oriental bukidnon the cotabato river basin davao region and the agusan river basin as heavy rains brought by the tail-end of the cold front tecf poured in the mountains of these areas floodwaters rushed down causing rivers to overflow destroying crops and properties hardest hit was the agusan river basin area which stretches from the mountains of davao where mining and logging operations destroyed the forest cover to butuan city up north floods turned thousands of hectares of farmlands into a virtual sea affecting thousands of farming families when i visited the flood-hit areas and consulted with local leaders thursday and friday local leaders and stakeholders agreed that unless something is done fast a disaster worse than what these areas are suffering from now could happen anytime aside from the emergency relief and rehabilitation efforts to be implemented by government there are at least two very important measures which must be started un the duterte presidency first dredging operations in the heavily silted rivers of the different river basins in the country especially agusan river the rio grande de mindanao in the cotabato river text_content: edit honestly after reading all the comments and seeing different experiences from fellow dabawenyos i think people are missing the point of what many of us are trying to say first of all nobody is saying okay lang ang baha if your house got flooded appliances destroyed no electricity no sleep lapok everywhere stranded for hours or years of hard work damaged overnight of course magreklamo ka valid kaayo na people deserve empathy first before politics and arguments but at the same time people also need to stop pretending that this flooding happened out of nowhere or that weather had zero contribution since may 17 pa unstable ang weather sa davao then may 18 to may 19 halos nonstop moderate to heavy rainfall with thunderstorms and flood advisories especially sa low-lying areas hours and almost days gyud nga ulan dili ni ordinary nga saglit lang nga ulan and yes flood control and drainage systems should continue improving nobody is against accountability nobody is saying perfect ang governance or flood response in fact people have every right to demand better drainage better urban planning better waste management better flood mitigation and better disaster response pero unfair pud nga murag naay baha walay gihimo or weather had nothing to do with it even the php 51 billion flood control nga sigeg balik online is misleading without context reports already clarified that the budget included roads bridges drainage works river defense projects coastal roads and other infrastructure gikan 2020-2022 dili siya one giant instant anti-baha project nga pag human impossible na dayon ang flooding forever and people forget davao's geography plays a huge role water runoff gikan mt apo side and nearby upland areas naturally drains toward the city and low-lying coastal areas once nonstop kusog ang ulan for hours or days certain areas will naturally become vulnerable especially flood-prone locations kami gani from matina gravahan near davao river usually dali gyud mi maigo pag inani nga weather but this time around compared before thankfully wala mi naigo badly despite the amount of rain so clearly there are mitigation efforts helping in some areas even if kulang pa gihapon overall even advanced countries like japan singapore and the netherlands still experience flooding during extreme rainfall despite decades of engineering and massive budgets flood mitigation reduces risk and damage it is not magic flood immunity at the end of the day criticism is valid demanding accountability is valid wanting better solutions is valid pero maybe stop turning every weather event into pure political hatebait while ignoring the actual weather conditions geography and complexity of the problem amping ta tanan kay sige pa gihapon ang ulan dds
